== History ==
According to the shrine's legend, it was founded in {{ill|Taihō (era)|ca|Taiho|de|Taihō (Ära)|es|Taihō (era)|fa|تایهو (دوره)|fr|Ère Taihō|ia|Taiho|id|Taihō|ja|大宝 (日本)|ko|다이호|pt|Taihō (era)|ru|Тайхо (нэнго)|simple|Taihō (era)|sr|Таихо (ера)|th|ไทโฮ (ศักราช)|tr|Taihō (dönem)|uk|Тайхо (ненґо)|zh|大宝 (日本)|zh_yue|大寶 (日本)|qid=Q1346269|lt=Taiho}} 3rd year ({{ill|703|ab|703|af|703|am|703 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|703|ar|703|ary|703|ast|703|avk|703|az|703|azb|۷۰۳ (میلادی)|bar|703|be|703|be_x_old|703|bg|703|bn|৭০৩|bpy|মারি ৭০৩|br|703|bs|703.|ca|703|cdo|703 nièng|ceb|703|ckb|٧٠٣|crh|703|cs|703|cv|703|cy|703|da|703|de|703|el|703|eml|703|eo|703|es|703|et|703|eu|703|fa|۷۰۳ (میلادی)|fi|703|fo|703|fr|703|fy|703|ga|703|gan|703年|gd|703|gl|703|he|703|hi|703|hr|703.|ht|703 (almanak jilyen)|hu|703|hy|703|id|703|ilo|703|io|703|is|703|it|703|ja|703年|jv|703|ka|703|kaa|703|kk|703 жыл|ko|703년|la|703|lb|703|lij|703|lmo|703|lt|703 m.|map_bms|703|mdf|703|mg|703|mhr|703|mk|703|mr|इ.स. ७०३|mrj|703 и|ms|703|mzn|۷۰۳|nah|703|nap|703|nds|703|new|सन् ७०३|nl|703|nn|703|no|703|nrm|703|nso|703|oc|703|or|୭୦୩|os|703-æм аз|pl|703|pnb|703|pt|703|qu|703|ro|703|ru|703 год|rue|703|sa|७०३|scn|703|sd|703ع|sh|703.|shn|703|si|703|sk|703|sl|703|sq|703|sr|703|su|703|sv|703|sw|703|tg|Соли 703|th|พ.ศ. 1246|tk|703|tl|703|tly|703|tr|703|tt|703 ел|uk|703|ur|703ء|uz|703|vec|703|vi|703|war|703|wuu|703年|xmf|703|zh|703年|zh_min_nan|703 nî|zh_yue|703年|qid=Q23500}}) by Masato Miyake, Tajihima, who was the envoy to the Tozando Chinpushu. One theory says that it was founded by {{ill|Emperor Seimu|ar|الإمبراطور سيمو|arz|الامبراطور سيمو|azb|سیمو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Seimu|cs|Seimu|de|Seimu|es|Seimu Tennō|fa|امپراتور سیمو|fi|Seimu|fr|Seimu|hr|Seimu|hu|Szeimu japán császár|id|Kaisar Seimu|it|Seimu|ja|成務天皇|ka|სეიმუ|ko|세이무 천황|nl|Seimu|pl|Seimu|pt|Seimu|ru|Император Сэйму|sh|Car Seimu|simple|Emperor Seimu|sl|Cesar Sejmu|sv|Seimu|th|จักรพรรดิเซมุ|tl|Emperador Seimu|tr|Seimu (imparator)|uk|Імператор Сейму|uz|Imperator Seimu|vi|Thiên hoàng Seimu|yo|Emperor Seimu|zh|成務天皇|zh_min_nan|Seimu Thian-hông|zh_yue|成務天皇|qid=Q316672}}6, by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Musashi Kunizo}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=older brother Tagehi no Mikoto}}. In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as ``{{ill|Musashi Province|ar|محافظة موساشي|ca|Província de Musashi|ckb|پارێزگای موساشی|cs|Provincie Musaši|de|Provinz Musashi|eo|Provinco Musaŝi|es|Provincia de Musashi|fa|ولایت موساشی|fr|Province de Musashi|gl|Provincia de Musashi|hak|Musashi-koet|id|Provinsi Musashi|it|Musashi (provincia)|ja|武蔵国|ko|무사시국|lt|Musašio žemė|nl|Musashi (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Musashi|pt|Província de Musashi|ru|Мусаси (провинция)|simple|Musashi Province|sk|Musaši (provincia)|sr|Провинција Мусаши|th|แคว้นมูซาชิ|tr|Musashi (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Мусаші|vi|Musashi (tỉnh)|zh|武藏國|zh_min_nan|Musasi-kok|zh_yue|武藏國|qid=Q907398}}{{ill|Saitama district|de|Saitama-gun|ja|埼玉郡|ko|사이타마군|uk|Повіт Сайтама|qid=Q11427160}} Tamashiki Shrine'' and is ranked as a small shrine.

== Main festivals ==

* January 1st
** New Year's Day Festival
** Saidan Festival
*February 1st
** Early spring festival, Kagura performance, Daruma market
** Daruma dolls are sold on this day every year, and you can also watch the votive dance<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=Sakitama Bunko・26
Tamashiki Shrine |date=1991-04-20 |year=1991 |publisher=Sanshodo Printing Co., Ltd. |page=26}}</ref>.
*February: Setsubun Festival, bean-throwing, prayers to ward off evil spirits
* Late April horse ride
** Ouma-kuguri was a practice in which children would pass under the bellies of two horses during a measles outbreak before the war to prevent children from contracting the measles and becoming seriously ill. After the war, this event was no longer observed as measles was no longer prevalent. However, after the war, it was revived as a wish for children's health and growth.<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=Sakitama Bunko・26
Tamashiki Shrine |date=1991-04-20 |year=1991 |publisher=Sanshodo Printing Co., Ltd. |pages=30-31}}</ref>.
** There are two sacred horse statues, one with the inscription of March auspicious day in {{ill|1785|ab|1785|af|1785|als|1785|am|1785 * Last Sunday of June: Go through the grass ring
*July 15th Summer Festival/Kagura Performance
* December 1st Annual festival/Kagura performance
* From January to November, Shishi-sama* Sometimes referred to as "Oshisama", it is a unique purification event and sacred treasure of Tamashiki Shrine. The lion, which is a sacred treasure of Tamashiki Shrine, is lent out to various places to pray for good harvests and family safety, and it is made up of a mask of Sarutahiko and a sacred treasure, a sword. |page=23}}</ref>. An example of a common method of worship is to enshrine each lion in front of a local shrine, and after the lion is enshrined, the event goes around the village to purify the lion.<ref name=":0" /> The area where this type of worship is practiced spreads mainly to the municipalities along the Moto-Arakawa River, which flows through the northeastern part of the prefecture, and extends to the towns of Tamamura and Itakura in Gunma Prefecture.  The purpose of the prayer varies depending on the season, and in the spring it is held to ward off disasters and to pray for a good harvest, and in the fall it is held to pray for good health.* Omizutori 1st of every month 7:00-16:00
** It is natural underground water and has been considered to be a sacred water with medicinal properties since the early Edo period.

== Cultural assets ==

=== Important intangible folk cultural property (designated by the country) ===* Tamashiki Shrine Kagura - Dedications are held at the early spring festival on February 1st, the spring festival on May 5th, the summer festival on July 15th, and the annual festival on December 1st. |language=ja-JP}}</ref>. It is performed in the Kagura hall located on the left hand side of the main shrine. <ref>{{Cite book|Japanese book |title=Sakitama Bunko 26 Tamashiki Shrine |date=1991-04-20 |publisher=Sakitama Publishing Co., Ltd. |page=12}}</ref>The shrine parishioners of the Masanori area have passed down the tradition from father to son. == Cultural property designated by Kazo City ==
*Tangible cultural property
** Tamashiki Shrine Kagura Hall - Designated on March 16, 1992.
** Tamashiki Shrine Document - Designated March 16, 1992 (Heisei 4).
*Tangible folk cultural properties
** Tamashiki Shrine Sangaku - Geometry problems written on frames or votive tablets are called Sangaku, and the one at Tamashiki Shrine has 15 questions. Designated on September 30, 1980.
** Large Ema for Kagura-ko - A 180cm wide x 151cm tall votive dedicated in 1848 (5th year of Koka). It depicts the scene before Kagura begins, when offerings are made to a shrine.<ref>{{Cite book|Japanese book|title=Tamamusubi Kiko|date=2021-08|publisher=Religious Corporation Tamashiki Shrine |pages=33-34}}</ref>. Designated on March 31, 1988.

* Natural monument
** Ginkgo of Tamashiki Shrine - Designated on March 31, 1988 (Showa 63).
